clue.text: Ultimately, holiness affected devil

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the following word, so only its final letter is wanted

parts.note: the closing letter of holiness
camp means theatrically affected or mannered

explanation.surface: A saint's holiness turns out to be an act put on by a demon.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous child is playfully called a little devil or rascal, which is exactly this word.

clue.text: Otherwise dunked in tea, buns served here?

indicators.note: something dunked in a drink is surrounded by it, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: cha is an informal British word for tea
or else means otherwise

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether buns dunked in tea are served in a particular café.
explanation.walkthrough: A Chelsea bun is a sticky currant bun named after the London district, so the question mark flags a place defined by what it bakes.
explanation.definitionFit: The London district gave its name to a famous spiral currant pastry, so a cryptic hint at baked goods points to it.

clue.text: Chicanery a concern for primates?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: mischievous or underhand behaviour
second meaning, read literally: an enterprise run by apes

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition takes the idiom at face value, with a concern meaning a firm, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes trickery or mischief, while taken literally it is a company whose staff are apes.

clue.text: Speedy writer

definitions.meaning: second meaning: Jonathan ..., author of Gulliver's Travels

explanation.surface: A description of an author who works fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means rapid, and the surname belongs to the Irish satirist behind Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: Monster story?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a big lie, a tall tale

explanation.surface: It looks like a request for a scary tale about a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the word means anything huge, and also a blatant falsehood or tall tale.

clue.text: One is foul, wicked criminal

indicators.note: wicked suggests something twisted and corrupted, so the preceding letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these three words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A judgement on a lawbreaker: this one is foul and wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Felonious is the legal adjective for something relating to a felony, so it is a synonym of criminal.

clue.text: Test right, scratching head

indicators.note: scratching out the head of a word removes its first letter

parts.note: moral means right, ethically correct

explanation.surface: Someone gets a test right while scratching their head in thought.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken examination, as in a language exam, is called an oral, a noun synonym for a test.

clue.text: Carried by old cook, starter of fillet coming up, meat dish

indicators.note: what is carried by something sits inside it, so these pieces go within the cook's name

parts.note: Mrs Beeton, the Victorian cookery writer

indicators.note: a starter is the first course, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: first letter of fillet
welling up means rising or coming up, like tears

explanation.surface: A recipe note: a Victorian cook's fillet starter arrives, then the main meat dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Isabella Beeton wrote the Victorian Book of Household Management, Britain's most famous old cookery book.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a classic dish of beef fillet coated in pâté and baked in puff pastry.

clue.text: Order without charge, unopened after month

indicators.note: something unopened has lost its opening, so the first letter goes

parts.note: Dec is the calendar abbreviation for December
free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: An order delivered free of charge, unopened, a month later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after month' places the shortened word after the month, so the month comes first in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree is an official order or edict issued by an authority such as a ruler or court.

clue.text: An older, funny old artist

indicators.note: funny suggests odd or peculiar, so the letters are put into a strange new order

parts.note: taken as written
O is a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A description of an elderly, amusing old painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci, painter of the Mona Lisa, is among the most celebrated Renaissance painters.

clue.text: Songs principal heard?

indicators.note: heard tells us to go by the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: a principal is a leader, the person in charge

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the songs were heard by the head teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs, typically Romantic poems set for voice and piano by Schubert or Schumann.

clue.text: Wife bitten by a hawk too

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: what is bitten is held between the jaws, so one letter sits inside another word

parts.note: to hawk goods is to sell them on the street
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Someone's wife has also been bitten by a hawk, the bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hawk' looks like the bird but is the verb meaning to peddle.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in addition or also, so it substitutes directly for the adverb too.

clue.text: A pro wearing long apron

indicators.note: something wearing a garment has it wrapped around it, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to pine is to long for
taken as written
pro means in favour of, for

explanation.surface: A professional is dressed in a long apron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective describing the apron but is the verb meaning to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is a sleeveless apron-like garment worn over clothes to keep them clean.

clue.text: Judge terribly irate with gutless barrister

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly mangled, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without its guts a word loses all its inner letters, leaving just the outside pair

parts.note: the first and last letters of barrister

explanation.surface: A judge is furious with a cowardly barrister in court.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is someone appointed to settle a dispute, so the noun is a synonym for a judge or referee.

clue.text: Witness provided, one residing in another street

indicators.note: someone residing in a place is housed inside it, so these letters go within the other word
another version of a word is a different arrangement of the same letters

parts.note: taken as written
if means provided that
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A witness has been supplied: someone who lives on a different road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another street' reads like a different road, but it asks for the letters of street rearranged as TESTER, which then holds IF and I.
explanation.definitionFit: One who gives evidence under oath in court is a witness, so the noun is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Key: one of two in first

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something that unlocks or opens
second meaning: a cricket batsman, one of the pair who go in to bat first

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket two batsmen start each innings together; each is called by this name. The colon makes 'Key' look like a heading.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool such as a tin or bottle device unlocks things, and in cricket the term names each starting batsman.

clue.text: Lack of action in vampires is at sunrise, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
in tells us the letters lie inside the following words, running across their boundaries

parts.note: the letters straddling the end of vampires, is, at and the start of sunrise

explanation.surface: Vampires famously fall still when the sun comes up, and a mirror reflection is a nice vampire touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of inactivity or equilibrium in which nothing changes, a noun meaning lack of action.

clue.text: Fat, everyone aboard tug

indicators.note: passengers aboard a vessel are inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: to tug is to tow or pull
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A heavy crew: everyone on board a tugboat is fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tug' looks like the boat, but it is the verb meaning to pull.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallow is hard animal fat, rendered from suet and used to make candles and soap.

clue.text: Show lips quivering during hours of sunlight?

indicators.note: during means within a stretch of time, so these letters fall inside the time word

parts.note: the day is the period of sunlight

indicators.note: quivering means trembling and unsettled, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shows trembling lips while out in the daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: A display is an exhibition or demonstration, so as a noun or verb it is a synonym for show.

clue.text: Snapper, like one on river

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it
I is the Roman numeral one
the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A fish compared to something found on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snapper' suggests the fish, but it is a camera that snaps pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A digital camera takes snaps, so the informal name for it fits a playful word for a camera.

clue.text: A cart drawn up on outskirts of Grasmere, distance measured

indicators.note: in a down entry something drawn up is pulled from bottom to top, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a dray is a heavy cart, used by brewers

indicators.note: the outskirts are the edges of a place, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Grasmere

explanation.surface: A horse and cart pulls up near Grasmere, a Lake District village, after a measured journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardage is a distance or length expressed in yards, as in golf or American football.

clue.text: Man after map in wood

parts.note: a plan is a map or diagram
a man is a piece in chess, and the king is one

explanation.surface: A man follows a map through a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man after map' puts the man word second. In crosswords a man is often a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Planking is timber cut into planks, especially boards laid for a floor or deck, so it is wood.

clue.text: Supportive framework required, test on horse backfiring

indicators.note: something backfiring goes the wrong way, so the word is turned back to front

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
to try is to test

explanation.surface: A rig is needed to trial a horse that keeps going wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'test on horse' places the test word after the horse word.
explanation.definitionFit: A gantry is a bridge-like overhead structure supporting cranes, signals or rocket launch equipment.

clue.text: Pure gunk on top of dustbin

parts.note: goo is sticky gunk

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down entry is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of dustbin

explanation.surface: Pure gunk sits on top of the rubbish bin.
explanation.definitionFit: Good in the moral sense means virtuous or innocent, close in meaning to pure.

clue.text: Little growth in a bison after mutation

indicators.note: a mutation is a change in form, so the letters come out altered in order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bison develops a small growth after a genetic mutation.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonsai is the Japanese art of growing miniature trees, so a dwarf tree is a little growth.

clue.text: An actor I cast, European

indicators.note: cast means thrown or moulded, so the letters are tossed into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A director casts an actor from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia is a country in south-east Europe, so a native of it is one kind of European.

clue.text: Best two or three, for example?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: numbers divisible only by themselves and one

explanation.walkthrough: 'two or three' sounds like a vague handful, but they are examples of a kind of number.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means top quality, as in prime beef, and 2 and 3 are both prime numbers.

clue.text: Range analysed, naturally dropping back somewhat

indicators.note: dropping back means moving in the opposite direction, so the letters are read right to left
somewhat means a portion only, so part of the following words holds the letters

parts.note: letters straddling the end of analysed and the start of naturally

explanation.surface: A mountain range is studied and naturally falls back a bit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are the long mountain range running down the western side of South America.
